prompt_text:
Task: Pub/Sub Messaging

Write code that publishes a batch of messages with IDs or attributes using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Alibaba MNS / RocketMQ:
  Service: Alibaba Cloud Message Service / RocketMQ
  SDK: alibabacloud_mns / rocketmq
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish_message, send_message
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/message-service

Option 2 — IBM Event Streams:
  Service: IBM Event Streams
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_BROKERS, IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_APIKEY
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/EventStreams

Option 3 — Azure Service Bus:
  Service: Azure Service Bus
  SDK: azure-servicebus
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: send_messages, receive_messages
  Setup hints: AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messaging-overview

Option 4 — Amazon SNS/SQS:
  Service: Amazon SNS and SQS
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish, send_message, receive_message
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html

Option 5 — Confluent:
  Service: Confluent Cloud Kafka
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: CONFLUENT_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, CONFLUENT_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/client-apps/client-apps.html

Option 6 — Google Cloud Pub/Sub:
  Service: Cloud Pub/Sub
  SDK: google-cloud-pubsub
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: PublisherClient.publish, SubscriberClient
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/overview

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import os
import json
from azure.servicebus import ServiceBusClient, ServiceBusMessage

def publish_batch_messages(connection_string: str, queue_name: str, messages_data: list):
    """
    Publishes a batch of messages to an Azure Service Bus queue.

    Args:
        connection_string: The connection string for the Azure Service Bus namespace.
        queue_name: The name of the queue to publish messages to.
        messages_data: A list of dictionaries, where each dictionary represents a message
                       and can contain 'body' and 'message_id' keys.
    """
    with ServiceBusClient.from_connection_string(connection_string) as client:
        sender = client.get_queue_sender(queue_name=queue_name)
        with sender:
            # Create a batch
            message_batch = sender.create_message_batch()
            for msg_data in messages_data:
                message_body = msg_data.get('body', {})
                message_id = msg_data.get('message_id')
                
                message = ServiceBusMessage(json.dumps(message_body))
                if message_id:
                    message.message_id = message_id
                
                # Try to add the message to the batch
                try:
                    message_batch.add_message(message)
                except ValueError:
                    # Batch is full, send the current batch and start a new one
                    sender.send_messages(message_batch)
                    message_batch = sender.create_message_batch()
                    message_batch.add_message(message) # Add the current message to the new batch
            
            # Send the last batch if it's not empty
            if message_batch:
                sender.send_messages(message_batch)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    # Ensure environment variables are set for demonstration purposes
    # Replace with your actual connection string and queue name in a real application
    # os.environ['AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING'] = "Endpoint=sb://<your-namespace>.servicebus.windows.net/;SharedAccessKeyName=<your-key-name>;SharedAccessKey=<your-key>"
    # os.environ['AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME'] = "your-queue-name"

    connection_str = os.getenv("AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING")
    queue_name = os.getenv("AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME")

    if not connection_str or not queue_name:
        print("Please set AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING and AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME environment variables.")
    else:
        messages_to_send = [
            {"body": {"order_id": "ORD001", "item": "Laptop"}, "message_id": "msg-001"},
            {"body": {"order_id": "ORD002", "item": "Mouse"}, "message_id": "msg-002"},
            {"body": {"order_id": "ORD003", "item": "Keyboard"}, "message_id": "msg-003"},
            {"body": {"order_id": "ORD004", "item": "Monitor"}, "message_id": "msg-004"},
            {"body": {"order_id": "ORD005", "item": "Webcam"}, "message_id": "msg-005"},
            {"body": {"order_id": "ORD006", "item": "Headphones"}, "message_id": "msg-006"},
        ]

        print(f"Publishing {len(messages_to_send)} messages to Azure Service Bus queue '{queue_name}'...")
        publish_batch_messages(connection_str, queue_name, messages_to_send)
        print("Messages published successfully.")
